images.title: One line of equal points
images.purpose: Recap that every meeting point of equal arcs from X and Y falls on one line, the perpendicular bisector.
images.composition: XY horizontal across the middle; four arc crossings stacked on one vertical line through the middle, generous white space left and right.
exact_structure: A horizontal dark segment XY in the middle of the frame, dots and labels X (left) and Y (right).
Four green (#009E73) dots on a vertical line through the midpoint of XY: two above XY at different heights and two below XY at different heights.

At each green dot, two short grey (#6B7280) arc pieces cross, one centred at X and one centred at Y, of the same radius for that dot; the four dots use four different radii, all more than half of XY. That is 8 short arc pieces in all.
A thin dashed reddish purple (#CC79A7) vertical line through all four green dots, crossing XY at its midpoint with a small square right angle mark.
One short caption line at the bottom of the frame.
labels: Equally far from X and Y
rejection: a green dot that is not on the reddish purple line, or other than 4 green dots
other than 8 arc pieces, or a pair of arcs crossing at a point with no green dot
the line not meeting XY at its midpoint
images.takeaway: Every point equally far from X and Y sits on one line that cuts XY in half at a right angle.
images.description: Four green arc crossing points, two above and two below XY, all lined up on one dashed vertical line through the midpoint of XY.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Use it as a recap before the practice: every new pair of equal arcs adds another dot on the same line.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap visual of the topic's key fact helps before students place their own points.
